categories_thin: Independent hotels: none found. In-town lodging on Route 18 and Tower Center Blvd is entirely branded (Best Western, Hilton, Holiday Inn Express, Residence Inn), so nothing qualifies.
Bookstores: only Barnes & Noble (chain) at Brunswick Square; no independent bookstore found.
Craft and hobby retail: no independent craft store in town; nearest is a chain Michaels in North Brunswick. The only hobby retail is Universal Comics & Hobbies and IRL Game Shop (games).
Hardware: no standalone independent hardware store; the independent option is the family-owned 18 Lumber yard (paint, hardware, millwork).
Tutoring and test prep: dominated by franchises (Huntington, Kumon, C2 Education, Genie Academy, PALS) which are excluded, so only Solution Prep and school-run programs remain.
Self-storage and moving: in-town self-storage is branded (CubeSmart, Public Storage, U-Haul); the movers surfaced are franchises or based outside town.
Event venues: mostly halls run by fraternal/civic organisations plus Palmeras (now categorised as a family entertainment centre), so this category is genuinely small.

Furniture: re-searched after the verifier flagged it, but still only four in-town independents (GMI Designs, Futon Corner, Baby & Kids Bedroom Gallery, A. Lammers). Everything else on Route 18 is a chain showroom.

Florists and garden centres: re-searched and improved (five florists, four garden centres/nurseries), but several entries rest on a single directory or a state agricultural list rather than a live website.
caveats: Zone is the township of East Brunswick only. Businesses in Milltown, North Brunswick, South River, Old Bridge and Spotswood that appeared in 'near East Brunswick' searches were excluded even though they are within 10 miles of central Milltown.

Chain rule applied strictly this round. Removed as chains/regional groups: Monmouth Cards (own store locator shows ~10 stores in NJ, CT and MA plus coming-soon units), Party Fair (multi-store NJ chain), Dade Paper Tri-State (branch of a multi-state distributor), The Barker Lounge retained only because it is a small NJ group - if the owner wants a single consistent rule, the Barker Lounge and Nice Guys Appliance are the remaining multi-location entries in this list.

Removed after verification could not support them: Lady K Jewels Boutique (directory marks the mall location closed), Toy Republic (address was wrong and the mall listing is closed; also a four-mall group), Greenfield Jewelers (only a 2004 newspaper ad; the obvious .com belongs to an unrelated Pittsburgh store), Lavon Art Gallery (1991 listing for a mall that no longer exists), Hy-Way Music Mart (reported closed March 2023), Allure Jewelry & Watches (own site now shows Bell Works, Holmdel), Alpine Medical & Surgical Supply (a directory marks it closed), Walther Electric (now Somerset), Cen-Med Enterprises (now New Brunswick), International Sea & Air Shipping (now North Bergen), IQ Direct (site now shows Valley Cottage, NY), Diamond K Dance (own site now gives a South Brunswick address), Route 18 Indoor Market (described as a former flea market), Niki International (only a bankruptcy service list), Priority Express, Industrial Pump Service, Distribution Warehouse & Service, Innovative Document Imaging, and East Brunswick Appliance Repair (same address listed under another name - likely lead-generation).
View A Miracle at 350 Cranbury Rd was dropped because the verifier's category was wrong: it is a pregnancy ultrasound studio, not a gift shop, and is outside this group-D zone.
Brunswick Memorial Home and Mount Sinai Memorial Chapels are now one entry sharing 454 Cranbury Rd; whether they are one operation could not be confirmed.

The Aldersgate thrift store is the one deliberate exception to the places-of-worship exclusion (public retail storefront, regular hours); the Unitarian Montessori School sits in a congregation building but is an independent school.
Brunswick Square Mall (755 Route 18) is being redeveloped; IRL Game Shop and Repairs By Nathan are mall tenants and may relocate, so confirm addresses before outreach.

Bulk-directory industrial/wholesale names were re-checked one by one this round. Most now carry a second source (own website, BBB, FMCSA, Macrae's, state directory) and are labelled accordingly, but corroboration of an address is not proof the site is still operating - the triage team should still confirm by phone.

Where a phone number or street address was not shown in any listing actually seen, the field says Unknown rather than guessing. No website is recorded unless it was seen linked from a listing or opened.

Two listings at 78 Summerhill Rd (Razor Printing and Rapid Print & Copy) may be the same shop under two names; likewise Futon Corner and GMI Designs share a phone number in one directory. Merge if confirmed.
data_gaps: Yellow Pages, Superpages, Cylex, ChamberofCommerce.com, WhereOrg, Manta, BBB category pages and Cybo returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching, so their lists were visible only through search-result snippets (typically the top 5-10 businesses per category).
Google Maps and Bing Maps were not usable from this environment, so no map-based completeness check with review recency was possible.

The East Brunswick Regional Chamber of Commerce member directory (ebrcc.org) is a JavaScript app that could not be scraped; it likely lists local retailers, services and manufacturers not captured here.
The NJ licensed child-care dataset returned no rows for East Brunswick, so licensed home daycares (which would be personal addresses) were not enumerated; only centre-based programs are listed.
Manufacturers are probably undercounted: D&B, Manta and Thomasnet detail pages were blocked, so several industrial names rest on bulk directories plus one corroborating record.
palmerasentertainment.com and palmerasbowling.com both failed DNS resolution here, so the venue's own site, hours and phone could not be checked; only the Patch opening article was available.
No source allowed confirming recent customer reviews for most entries, so 'active_evidence' reflects own websites and current directory presence rather than activity timestamps.

Some published addresses (Commerce Sign Solutions, Lifetyme, Rob Wilson Photography, Fred's Furniture Repair, Kids Stuff Consignments, Anita's Wags to Riches) look like home-based studios; only the street address as published in business directories is recorded, and triage should treat them as owner-operated.
